title: Anvil unified audit record v1 (SARIF 2.1.0 + anvil/* extension)
description: Constrains the anvil/* property-bag extension that Anvil layers on top of stock SARIF 2.1.0, and pins the SARIF-native slots Anvil depends on. Ground truth: plan/design/record-and-store.md 'Record Field Contract'; enum literals frozen by the first plan's shared-vocabulary review; required fields by the spine's record section. Producer/consumer for every field: internal/record/CONTRACT.md. Go source of truth: internal/record/contract.go.
x-anvil-validationProcedure: TWO GATES, both required. Gate 1: validate the record against https://json.schemastore.org/sarif-2.1.0.json (stock SARIF conformance; needed for GitHub and DefectDojo to accept it). Gate 2: validate against THIS schema (the anvil/* extension and the S6-required fields). This schema does not $ref the SARIF base schema because that reference is not resolvable in Anvil's offline CI; keeping the two gates separate makes the offline gate work and makes a SARIF-conformance failure distinguishable from an anvil/* failure.

$schema.description: Pinned to SARIF 2.1.0. Do not track the unratified 2.2 draft (research/18 Risk #9).

runs.description: One audit identity, two independently-sealed halves (the spine's corrected-requirements table). At most one run per half.

state.description: FROZEN ENUM 1/6 (anvil/state). dast_sealed and both_sealed exist because the spine's corrected-requirements table requires two INDEPENDENTLY-sealed halves: a machine that can only seal SAST-then-DAST cannot express a DAST-first seal, and collapsing them makes `sealed` terminal, which makes `consumed` unreachable.

halfStatus.description: FROZEN ENUM 2/6 (per-half anvil/status). `sealed` is the hard consumer read gate (the sealer); an area keying on any other token means the gate never opens.

dastStatus.description: FROZEN ENUM 3/6 (anvil/dastStatus). Never null. `skipped_no_manifest` is deliberately distinct from `not_run`: no target manifest was declared, versus the DAST tier not being installed at all. The spine's record section requires a target that failed to be distinguishable from one scanned clean; only `completed_clean` may be read as 'dynamically scanned, nothing found'.

targetProvenance.description: FROZEN ENUM 4/6 (anvil/target.provenance). The target's BOOT/REACHABILITY OUTCOME. dastStatus is derived from this field, not from target.provisioning.

targetProvisioning.description: FROZEN ENUM 5/6 (anvil/target.provisioning). Required unless target.provenance is no_target_declared, and absent then: both values describe how a runtime target came to exist. WHICH PROVISIONING PATH produced the target. A different measurement from target.provenance; merging them loses information the spine's record section requires, and the two carry different authorization consequences (the spine's safety section).

verdict.description: FROZEN ENUM 6/6 (anvil/verdict). `insufficient_context` is a real verdict, not a low confidence score (the spine's record section is explicit). A low score means 'probably not real'; insufficient_context means 'may well be real and the detector could not see enough to tell'. Those demand opposite handling and a float cannot express the difference. `unconfirmed` (added before the v1 freeze by the gate decision of 2026-10-03) is a recall rule match nothing has judged; the coding agent's triage gate decides it.

trust.description: anvil/trust (the spine's record section, required on EVERY string originating outside Anvil). A repo source snippet is `untrusted` even though Anvil put it in the struct: the question is who wrote the bytes, never who assigned the field.

externalTrust.description: The subset of anvil/trust legal for a string that originated outside Anvil. `anvil_generated` is excluded by construction.

specHarvestOutcome.description: What the SAST spec-harvest pass did. NOT one of the six frozen enums; the record area owns the vocabulary, the SAST half produces it and the repo spec reader consumes it, with the same two literals on both sides so the handoff needs no mapping. There is no member for the empty string: an empty file list under `harvest_ran` is a fact about the REPOSITORY, under `harvest_skipped` it is a fact about ANVIL, and the difference is the denominator of anvil/dastCoverage.endpointCoverage.

handoffState.description: Frozen alongside the six (the shared-vocabulary review's handoff-table and one-ledger rulings). Not carried on the wire record; declared here so the store DDL (the store schema) and remediation agree on one vocabulary and remediation's deleted anvil_ledger cannot reappear.

ruleProvenance.description: Record 1.1.0, anvil/ruleProvenance: where a rule came from, stated in full or not at all.

trustedString.description: An anvil/* extension string that originated outside Anvil, carrying its trust inline. SARIF-native strings cannot change shape, so those are classified by JSON Pointer in anvil/trust.fields instead.

anvil/version.description: Monotonic; a bump re-cuts the work queue (the spine's record section, the queue re-cut).

trigger.description: The record states WHICH configured policy fired. No trigger condition is ever encoded in the schema itself (research/18).

deadline.description: Replaces branch 18's anvil/buffer per the spine's corrected-requirements table correction: the 8 hours is a CLAIM TIMEOUT, not a deletion policy and not a confidentiality control. deadlineAt = scan start + claimTimeoutSeconds, computed once and never recomputed from any write timestamp.

dastDeadlineSeconds.description: An INDEPENDENT clock from claimTimeoutSeconds. Null when DAST is disabled.

index.description: Tier-0 manifest, target <= 8 KB. readOrder is deterministic, not model-chosen.

run.description: One independently-sealed half. Both runs carry the SAME automationDetails.correlationGuid, equal to anvil/auditId: the SARIF-native statement that they are one audit.

tool.description: SARIF tool. Record 1.1.0 constrains tool.extensions: the rule corpora and native analysers Lane B ran, each holding the rules its results cite, each rule stating anvil/ruleProvenance.

allOf.$comment: The DAST run must carry coverage, a route-table digest and its runtime target. Without dastCoverage, dastStatus:'completed_clean' is unfalsifiable.
The SAST run must carry the advisory snapshot digest it read, or staleness is unknowable.
The sealer's read gate: sealedAt is required exactly when status is sealed, and must be null otherwise. A missing key and an unsealed half must not be the same observation.

authProfileRef.description: A config file path and revision. The record NEVER carries credentials.

allOf.$comment: anvil/specHarvest is the SAST half's statement. plan/design/dynamic-tier.md:628-630 assigns spec harvesting to the SAST tier and forbids the DAST tier from re-deriving it, so a copy on the DAST run is a second durable statement of one fact — the shape the spine's corrected-requirements table and the one-ledger ruling both refuse.

specHarvest.description: run.properties["anvil/specHarvest"] — which API spec files the SAST pass harvested from the target repository, and WHETHER IT RAN AT ALL. An outcome, a file list and an omission count, never a bare file list: the interesting cases are all the ones where the list is short, and a short list with no accompanying statement is indistinguishable from a complete one. Absent means the record makes no statement, which is NOT the same as harvest_skipped.

files.$comment: null is admitted HERE only so the harvest_skipped branch can express it; the harvest_ran branch narrows it back to an array, which is where a null list and an empty list stop being the same observation.

omittedFileCount.description: How many spec files the harvest SAW and did NOT carry into `files`. Required under harvest_ran and explicitly `null` under harvest_skipped — never omitted, and never 0 by default: 0 asserts that `files` is COMPLETE, which is the permissive reading a forgetful producer would get free.

then.$comment: A null list and an empty list must not be the same observation.
A pass that did not run cannot have delivered files, and saw nothing to omit. `null` and `[]` are both legal here and mean the same thing, because there is no list to have been written down.

specHarvestFile.description: One harvested spec file. THE BYTES ARE ATTACKER-AUTHORED: a committed openapi.yaml, WSDL or Postman collection is written by whoever can commit to the scanned repository, and every network destination inside one is a repository-supplied address. Nothing here grants scope or authorization.

location.description: SARIF §3.4 artifactLocation naming the file in the target repository. A harvested file nobody can name is a file no operator can go look at when its routes turn out to be wrong.

sizeBytes.description: The file's exact length in bytes as harvested. Zero is legal: a repository may commit a zero-byte openapi.yaml, and refusing to record that would delete the file from the harvest list.

contentSha256.description: Lowercase-hex SHA-256 of the file's exact bytes AS HARVESTED, before any normalisation, re-encoding or YAML-to-JSON conversion. It states WHICH bytes the DAST tier parsed, so a re-run that produces a different route list can be told apart from a repository that changed.

content.description: SARIF §3.3 artifactContent. Optional, and when present it is the WHOLE file — text length must equal sizeBytes. There is no truncation flag on purpose: a silently truncated spec yields a short route list, which is a smaller coverage denominator, which makes endpoint_coverage look better than it is. Truncate out of band and elide this instead.

declaredFormat.description: What the HARVESTER claimed the file is. Recorded and never believed — the repo spec reader classifies from the bytes, because the harvester classifies on a path and the path is in the repository. Deliberately NOT an enum this schema freezes: the parser vocabulary is the dynamic tier's growing allowlist, and freezing a snapshot of it here would make every new parser a produce/consume break.

trust.description: Labels the URI, the declared format and the content. A spec file committed to the target repository is external text whatever Anvil did to assemble the struct around it, so `anvil_generated` is excluded by construction.

dastCoverage.description: Consolidates the spine's dast_coverage, endpoint_coverage and inventory_provenance. A numerator, a denominator and a provenance mix — never a bare ratio (research/14 critique m6). endpoint_coverage is confirmed-probed endpoints over the union of the Tier 0-2 inventory, NEVER a request count.

serverLineCoverage.description: Null, NOT zero, when not measured. Zero would read as 'we ran and covered nothing'.

rank.description: SARIF PRIORITY 0-100. NEVER confidence: detector certainty lives in anvil/confidence, and ingested third-party `rank` must be treated as untrusted and re-derived (research/18 Risk #8).

correlationGuid.description: Assigned per CLUSTER, not per finding. Present only on clustered findings.

rule.description: Record 1.1.0: the rule this result cites, by id and by its tool extension's index. internal/record checks that it resolves; this schema checks its shape.

fixes.description: Written only after a coding-agent proposal. The spine's safety section: never auto-merge, propose only.

primaryLocationLineHash.description: Required when a physical code location exists. The ONLY partial fingerprint GitHub reads.

regionSha256.description: research/24's fingerprint.region_sha256. Reserved, optional; the fingerprint decides whether to populate it. Logged deviation 2 in CONTRACT.md.

allOf.$comment: A host finding is never remediable by an agent. The spine's safety section: the host agent is read-only, not behind a flag. The store enforces the same rule with a CHECK constraint.
A DAST response body is up to 32 KB of attacker-controlled bytes headed for a repo-credentialed agent (the spine's safety section). Any result carrying one defaults to untrusted.

anvil/confidence.description: DETECTOR CERTAINTY in [0,1]. Distinct from SARIF rank (priority) and level (severity).

anvil/groupId.description: Key RESERVED here; ASSIGNED by the coding-agent consumption pipeline, not by this area.

trustAssertion.description: The spine's record section requires trust on EVERY string originating outside Anvil, and one result carries several strings of different provenance at once. `default` covers anything not named; `fields` maps an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer relative to the result object to that string's trust. Logged deviation 3 in CONTRACT.md.

validationStep.description: Names the explicit validation step behind every `verified` label in this result (default, fields, and the inline trust of an advisory excerpt, licence note or reproduction span). Required exactly when some label in the result is `verified`; the Go validator enforces that across the whole result, and this schema enforces it for `default`.

licenseSpdx.description: Carried per finding: the feed licence attaches to the text, not to Anvil (the spine's licence section).

excerpt.description: <= 800 tokens, pre-trimmed by ingestion, never a whole advisory. External text, so it carries its own trust inline.

licenseManualNote.description: The manual licence override: the QUOTED OPERATIVE SENTENCE from the publisher's own licence text, required by Lane A's licence gate whenever licenseSpdx is NONE, NOASSERTION or a LicenseRef- id — the population where the SPDX identifier establishes nothing. It sits beside the excerpt because it licenses the excerpt: the feed licence attaches to the TEXT, not to Anvil. A TrustedString and not a bare string, because a quotation from a publisher's LICENSE file originated outside Anvil; `anvil_generated` is excluded, and so is a blank note, which would satisfy "a note exists" while establishing nothing (the ingestion cache enforces length(trim(...)) > 0 in SQL). This slot does NOT make the record the enforcement point for the spine's licence section — that subject is the CI gate — it only makes the note survive into the record.

risk.description: research/24's non-negotiable ranking inputs. LOGGED DEVIATION 1: no row for anvil/risk exists in plan/design/record-and-store.md's Record Field Contract table.

buildCommand.description: Null or omitted when the language has no build step. Both spellings are accepted; Go's decoder treats null as absent.

correlation.description: LINK, NEVER MERGE. Both findings always survive independently: the SAST finding owns the file and line, the DAST finding owns the proof. >= 2 independent signals are required, and a CWE-only match is banned as a sole signal.

not.$comment: A CWE-only signal list is banned: CWE match is necessary, never sufficient.

allOf.$comment: The spine's safety section: only a response stack trace naming the SAST file, or a post-patch re-run that flips, earns verified:true. Confidence alone never qualifies.

match.description: A regex-extracted evidence SPAN, never the raw body (the spine's safety section: hash-and-reference by default). Attacker-controlled, so it carries its own trust inline.

env.description: The spine's record section requires sanitizer + ASLR state on any reproducer. A crash that reproduces only under ASan is a different claim from one that reproduces on a stock build, and a verification re-run under different settings is not the same experiment.

sanitizers.description: Empty array for a stock build. NEVER null: null cannot be distinguished from 'nobody recorded it'.
